title: Jointly private linear bandits with i.i.d. contexts.
summary: Each round reveals a context or action-feature set before an action is selected and its reward with linear mean is observed. The algorithm satisfies joint differential privacy, limiting the influence of one user's information on actions shown to other users. Contexts are i.i.d. from an unknown distribution.

model.instance: Contexts $x_t$ are i.i.d. from an unknown distribution $P$. The finite action set $\mathcal A$ and feature map $\phi$ are public. The fixed unknown parameter and features lie in the Euclidean unit ball: $$\|\phi(x,a)\|_2\le1,\quad\|\theta_\star\|_2\le1,\quad Y_t\in[-1,1],\quad\mathbb E[Y_t\mid x_t,a_t,\mathcal H_{t-1}]=\langle\phi(x_t,a_t),\theta_\star\rangle.$$ Rewards are fresh draws from the current conditional law. The learner observes the context, selects an action, and then receives that action's reward. $$d_{\mathcal A}=\max_x\dim\operatorname{span}\{\phi(x,a):a\in\mathcal A\}\le\min\{d,|\mathcal A|\}.$$

restrictions: Neighboring streams $\mathsf D,\mathsf D^{\prime}$ differ only in one user's context/reward pair. The protected output is every action except that user's current recommendation, received privately. For every measurable event $E$, require:
$$\Pr\!\left(\mathcal M(\mathsf D)_{-t}\in E\right)\le e^{\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}}}\Pr\!\left(\mathcal M(\mathsf D^{\prime})_{-t}\in E\right)+\delta_{\mathrm{priv}}.$$
The privacy relaxation constrains the entire output mechanism. Performance is measured in expectation, without a separate external statistical failure probability.

regimes.predicate_text: $d_{\mathcal A}=\max_x\dim\operatorname{span}\{\phi(x,a):a\in\mathcal A\}$ Contexts are i.i.d.; rewards and features satisfy the stated boundedness assumptions. The Gaussian privacy scale $\sigma_{\mathrm{priv}}$ is defined in Definition 3 of the source and is of order $\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_{\mathrm{priv}})}/\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}}$; it is distinct from reward noise. The bound states the window $0<\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}}\le1$ and $0<\delta_{\mathrm{priv}}\le1$, intersected with the privacy-parameter domain in the specification. If $d_{\mathcal A}=O(1)$, the displayed bound becomes $\widetilde O(\sqrt{dT}+d^{3/2}/\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}})$. The polynomial dimension factor cannot be omitted to claim that the $d/\epsilon_{\mathrm{priv}}$ dependence is resolved.
